newsitem.title: UK: N Sea Brent softer, other grades hold.
newsitem.headline: N Sea Brent softer, other grades hold.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil lost ground and looked set to fall further after two low deals on Monday. With some of the August programmes now out sweet North Sea barrels for this period have started to move and levels were holding well, traders said.
A July 27-29 Brent cargo was bought by a trader at August Brent -10 cents. Talk that the buyer then sold one million barrels around the same loading period could not be confirmed.
Later a July 17-19 Brent moved at August Brent -20 cents for a minimum sized cargo.
Monday's seller of Brent was seen with up to four further third decade cargoes on offer at August -10 cents with best bid at August -15 cents.
"The Brent market is being manipulated according to peoples CFD positions," one trader said adding that the current Aug Brent -15/-10 cent market was too low.

An August 3-5 Statfjord moved at dated Brent +37 cents while a refiner picked up an early August Gullfaks A cargo at a three cent premium to dated Brent. Talk of trade of a Gullfaks C loading around August 7-9 could not be confirmed.

All three July 29-31 loading Brent cargoes which turned wet today were kept - one by Shell U.K. and two by Stasco. The original schedule showed only one cargo due to load and the extra two are heard to have been put together from top-ups bringing the total number of full cargoes loading in July to 39, traders said.
As outright Brent levels on the IPE lost ground on the back of news on Iraq and of imminent sales of German strategic crude, CFDs and intermonth spreads came off.

U.N. coordinator in Baghdad, Staffan De Mistura, said on Monday that discussions about the food distribution plan were finalised and the whole process would be completed by next Monday though he would not speculate as to when oil sales from Iraq would resume.
The German Economics Ministry said the first tranche in its planned tender of strategic crude oil reserves in early August would be about 2.8 million barrels.

August Brent on the IPE had lost some 21 cents to trade at $17.88 a barrel by 1745 GMT. Late talk on the CFD market put this week at Sept -20/-15 cents and the July 21-25 at Sept -24/-21 cents. The July 21-25, July 28-01 roll traded earlier at +3.5 cents.
The August Brent programme was due to be released early on Tuesday. Traders expected it down just one or two cargoes from July. The August loading programme for Flotta was also expected on Tuesday.

Full details on the Turkish crude oil buy tender were slow to emerge but Tupras, Turkey's state oil refiner, was heard to have bought Iranian Heavy, Syrian Light and Tengez crude grades in the tender which closed on Monday. Tupras had originally looked for 300,000 tonnes of crude.
